name: brainstorming
description: Turns rough ideas into validated designs through dialogue. First classifies the request as a spike, a bounded change, or architectural work, then scales the process to match: a quick probe, a short design in chat, or a full written spec. Nothing is implemented until you approve.
whenToUse: Starting any new feature or project
Turning a rough idea into a spec

phases.label: Spike
phases.detail: A feasibility question. Claude states what it will try, investigates cheaply, and reports a recommendation. Any code is throwaway.

phases.label: Bounded
phases.detail: A well-scoped change to code that already exists. A few clarifying questions, a short design in chat, then your approval. No spec file.

phases.label: Architectural
phases.detail: New projects or restructuring. Questions one at a time, 2–3 approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec and an implementation plan.

name: writing-plans
description: Breaks an approved design into tasks, each with its own test cycle and an independently testable deliverable. Steps inside a task are bite-sized (2–5 min) with exact file paths, complete code, and verification commands. No placeholders, no TBDs.
whenToUse: After brainstorming produces an approved spec
Breaking complex work into trackable tasks

name: using-git-worktrees
description: Creates an isolated git worktree on a new branch so feature work won't contaminate the main workspace. Runs project setup and verifies a clean test baseline before work starts.
whenToUse: When you need isolation from current workspace

name: subagent-driven-development
description: Dispatches a fresh subagent per task from the implementation plan. A task reviewer checks spec compliance and code quality after each task, with up to five fix rounds. Ends with a whole-branch review. Can run autonomously for hours.

phases.label: Implement
phases.detail: A fresh implementer subagent reads the task, writes code with TDD, tests, commits, and self-reviews.

phases.label: Task review
phases.detail: A task reviewer checks the diff for spec compliance and code quality in one pass.

phases.label: Fix loop
phases.detail: Findings go back to the implementer for up to five rounds. Later rounds escalate to a fresh, more capable subagent.

phases.label: Final review
phases.detail: When every task is done, a whole-branch code review runs before handing off to finishing-a-development-branch.

name: executing-plans
description: Executes an implementation plan in the current session, task by task, stopping to ask whenever a blocker or unclear instruction appears. Intended for environments without subagents; when subagents are available, subagent-driven-development is preferred.
whenToUse: Executing a plan when subagents are not available
When you want to follow the plan step by step yourself

name: dispatching-parallel-agents
description: Fans out 2+ independent tasks to parallel subagents. Significantly faster than sequential execution when tasks have no shared state or sequential dependencies.
whenToUse: When sequential execution would be slow

name: test-driven-development
description: Enforces RED→GREEN→REFACTOR cycle. Write failing test first, confirm it fails, write minimal code to pass, refactor. Deletes code written before tests.
whenToUse: Implementing any feature or bug fix
Any time implementation code is written

phases.label: RED
phases.detail: Write a failing test that describes the desired behavior. Run it — confirm it fails.

phases.label: GREEN
phases.detail: Write the minimal implementation to make the test pass. No more than needed.

phases.label: REFACTOR
phases.detail: Clean up the code while keeping tests green. Improve names, remove duplication.

name: systematic-debugging
description: 4-phase root cause process. No fixes without root cause investigation first. If three fixes fail, Claude stops and questions the architecture instead of trying a fourth.
whenToUse: When the same bug keeps recurring

phases.label: Root cause investigation
phases.detail: Read errors fully, reproduce consistently, check recent changes, add diagnostics at component boundaries, trace bad data back to its source.

phases.label: Pattern analysis
phases.detail: Find working examples in the same codebase, read reference implementations completely, and list every difference from the broken code.

phases.label: Hypothesis and testing
phases.detail: State one specific hypothesis, test it with the smallest possible change, one variable at a time. Wrong? Form a new hypothesis, do not stack fixes.

phases.label: Implementation
phases.detail: Write a failing test that reproduces the bug, apply a single fix at the root cause, then verify with verification-before-completion.

name: verification-before-completion
description: Requires running the full verification command and reading its real output before claiming anything is done, fixed, or passing. Evidence before assertions, always.

phases.label: Run
phases.detail: Execute the full command, fresh and complete.

phases.label: Read
phases.detail: Read the whole output. Check the exit code. Count the failures.

phases.label: Claim
phases.detail: Only if the output confirms it, state the claim together with the evidence.

name: requesting-code-review
description: Dispatches a code-reviewer subagent that checks the changes against the plan or requirements. Reports strengths and issues by severity: Critical must be fixed now, Important before proceeding, Minor noted for later.
whenToUse: Between implementation tasks in a plan

name: receiving-code-review
description: Processes review feedback with technical rigor — verifies each suggestion is correct before implementing. Pushes back on incorrect feedback rather than blindly applying it.
whenToUse: When feedback seems unclear or questionable

name: finishing-a-development-branch
description: Verifies tests pass, then presents three options: merge locally, push and open a PR, or keep the branch as-is. Discards only if you ask. Cleans up the worktree afterwards. Won't merge until tests are confirmed green.
whenToUse: All tasks in the plan are complete

name: writing-skills
description: Complete guide for creating, testing, and deploying new skills. Covers skill types, SKILL.md structure, writing descriptions that trigger reliably, and adversarial pressure testing with subagents before deployment.
whenToUse: After mastering the core superpowers workflow

name: using-superpowers
description: The entry point that loads automatically at the start of every conversation. Establishes the rule that if a skill might apply, Claude must invoke it before responding, even before asking a clarifying question. Process skills like brainstorming and systematic-debugging come first, then implementation skills.
whenToUse: When you want to understand why Claude keeps invoking skills
When Claude skips a skill it should have used
